findings.text: follow-on: _ChainGraphClient.query re-implements the graph's bound-detection predicate (len(chain) > bound + 1, reporting chain[bound]) rather than exercising the Cypher, so no test reddens if the production query's boundary detection is reverted or altered - the query half of the fix (the EXISTS((member)-[:HAS_SUCCESSOR]->()) combined with the depth = _WAIVED_CHAIN_DEPTH_BOUND arm) has no regression guard, only the one-off EXPLAIN/property check the manifest cites. The Python refusal path it does exercise is guarded (negative control below).

follow-on: the focused-gate logs' first line stamps REV=57726eec9, the BASE revision, while each ran head code 3c43c98a0 (head_waiver.log contains the head-only test test_the_cut_reads_a_chain_reaching_exactly_the_bound_without_refusing; negative_control.log ran the bound-removed head code; cypher_property_check.log passed the new query), so the header does not name the revision the gate ran and a reader reconciling it against the manifest's head revision meets a mismatch.

follow-on: the recorded after_suite failure_ids lists 21 ids including a duplicate (test_review_release_scopes_dd_caveats_to_batch_names appears twice) while its failure_count field is 20, whereas the arm log logs/export_after.log carries exactly 20 FAILED lines; the archived id list should be the arm's 20 ids.

item_verdicts.call_sites: imas_codex/standard_names/export.py:3019 run_export calls the changed function before any staging output exists; run_export is reached from imas_codex/standard_names/catalog_release.py:2288 and imas_codex/cli/sn.py:4461 and :4610.
item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against base 57726eec9; the single commit 3c43c98a0 adds _WAIVED_CHAIN_DEPTH_BOUND and _refuse_waiver_chain_beyond_bound, rewrites the successor-chain query to detect the bound in-query, adds two tests plus the mock's bound mirroring, and writes the evidence fragment; no production module outside export.py is touched.
item_verdicts.done_when: the four done_when items resolve: tests/standard_names/test_export_waiver_intermediates.py adds test_the_cut_refuses_a_waived_source_whose_chain_exceeds_the_bound (over-long fixture) and test_the_cut_reads_a_chain_reaching_exactly_the_bound_without_refusing (within-bound as today); the first fails DID NOT RAISE with the bound check removed (logs/negative_control.log EXIT=1); the modified Cypher was run through tests/graph/test_cypher_property_check.py 4 passed EXIT=0 (logs/cypher_property_check.log) and an EXPLAIN against the live graph; the export set shows no added failure (base 19 failed/432 passed, head 20 failed/437 passed, every failure a 30s pytest-timeout in the untouched tests/standard_names/test_review_release.py).
item_verdicts.goal: the goal is that the export waiver refusal refuses at its traversal bound instead of returning a truncated successor-chain identity set; imas_codex/standard_names/export.py:2822 _fetch_waived_source_chain_identities now carries length(trail) AS depth and a CASE marking the member at the maximum depth that still has an outgoing HAS_SUCCESSOR, and imas_codex/standard_names/export.py:2878 raises through _refuse_waiver_chain_beyond_bound (export.py:2796) naming the source path and the identity at the bound, through the same WaivedSourceDeclarationError path the sibling refusal uses.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it records status complete, commit 3c43c98a0, the gate command, baseline_suite and after_suite with revision/exit_status/completed and failure ids, negative_control_log logs/negative_control.log, and follow_ons naming the unbounded sibling reader; every cited log exists on disk and reconciles with the claim except the three record defects in the findings (a base-stamped header on head-code logs, and one duplicated id in after_suite.failure_ids).
item_verdicts.write_paths: declared write paths are imas_codex/standard_names/export.py, tests/standard_names/test_export_waiver_intermediates.py and docs/evidence/fragments/sn-integrity-backlog/sib-export-chain-bound.html; git diff --stat 57726eec9..3c43c98a0 changes exactly those three (65/94/6 lines), all inside the fence and nothing outside it.

justifications.durability: the negative control reinstates the regression (bound check replaced by if False) and test_the_cut_refuses_a_waived_source_whose_chain_exceeds_the_bound reddens DID NOT RAISE (logs/negative_control.log EXIT=1), so the refusal branch is guarded; the query half is not, because _ChainGraphClient.query at tests/standard_names/test_export_waiver_intermediates.py:115 supplies boundary_identities from its own mirror of the Cypher predicate, so a reverted EXISTS/depth arm in the production query would leave every test green.
justifications.evidence: the gate measures the done_when and the result is recorded in named on-disk logs (logs/head_waiver.log 6 passed EXIT=0, logs/negative_control.log EXIT=1 DID NOT RAISE, logs/cypher_property_check.log 4 passed EXIT=0, logs/export_base_arm.log 19 failed/432 passed, logs/export_after.log 20 failed/437 passed), but the manifest's primary cited head log carries a base revision in its first line and the live reduced-cap demonstration is claimed with no log path, so the record is short of the revision-tagged standard.
justifications.fit: imas_codex/standard_names/export.py:2796 mirrors the shape of the sibling refusal helper _refuse_waiver_that_reached_a_name at export.py:2759 (sorted(set(...)), rendered repr join, same exception class), and the added names _WAIVED_CHAIN_DEPTH_BOUND and _refuse_waiver_chain_beyond_bound carry no plan or ticket label.
justifications.goal_fidelity: imas_codex/standard_names/export.py:2846-2878 detects the boundary in the same query (depth = _WAIVED_CHAIN_DEPTH_BOUND plus EXISTS((member)-[:HAS_SUCCESSOR]->())) and raises via export.py:2796, naming the source path and the identity at the bound exactly as the goal states, rather than returning a truncated set.
justifications.reuse: the new function extends the existing refusal capability rather than forking it, raising the same WaivedSourceDeclarationError the sibling refusal at imas_codex/standard_names/export.py:2759 raises; no other owner of bounded successor-chain reading exists in the module, and the unbounded sibling reader in imas_codex/standard_names/graph_ops.py is correctly left as a follow-on.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --stat 57726eec9..3c43c98a0 touches exactly the three declared source paths (export.py, the test file, the fragment html) and nothing else; the declared docs/figures directory is unused, no generated file is staged, and the out-of-scope graph_ops.py sibling reader is left untouched, named only under follow_ons.
